title: Build LearnPanel component
description:
Create `dashboard/frontend/components/landing/LearnPanel.tsx`.

Props: typed from the `learn` field of LandingViewData.

Sub-components:
- `PanelLabel` (imported): 'Learn' + 'Patterns and improvement'.
- `CoverageTrend`: list of feature rows. Each row: feature name (truncated to ~20 chars) + mini horizontal bar (max-width 100px, filled proportionally to `coveragePct`) + percentage in mono. Sorted by coverage descending.
- `Insights`: list of insight cards. Each card has a type indicator (green dot for 'good', amber dot for 'warn') + text. Max ~5 visible, no scroll needed for V1.
- `EscalationTrend`: list of feature rows with feature name + count badge. Higher counts get amber treatment.

Empty state: 'No learning data yet' when all sub-arrays are empty.

Layout: right sidebar, 320px width (controlled by parent grid), spans full height. Internal padding 20px. `.surface` class.
acceptance_criteria:
- CoverageTrend renders mini bars with widths proportional to coveragePct
  verify_by: test
- Insights render with correct green/amber dot based on type
  verify_by: test
- EscalationTrend renders feature names with count badges
  verify_by: test
- Empty state renders when all learn arrays are empty
  verify_by: test
- Coverage features sorted descending by percentage
  verify_by: test

spec_references.requirement: S6: Learn panel with coverage trends, insights, escalation trend

rationale: LearnPanel is read-only with no interactions, making it the simplest panel. Parallel with JudgePanel and ExecutePanel since they all only share the PanelLabel dependency from task 11.
decisions: Props are spread directly from LearnPanel type (matching task 17's expected usage: <LearnPanel {...data.learn} />)
Escalation amber threshold set at count >= 3 — 'higher counts' needs a concrete threshold; 3 is the smallest value that semantically reads as 'multiple escalations'
Feature name truncation uses CSS 'truncate' class + fixed maxWidth rather than JS substring — more robust for dynamic content
Insight dot uses aria-label (good/warning) for accessibility and test targeting, following the same pattern as PanelLabel tests
visibleInsights = insights.slice(0, 5) implements the 'max ~5 visible, no scroll needed for V1' requirement
concerns: Test framework (vitest + @testing-library/react) is not yet installed in the frontend — tests are syntactically correct but will not run until task 19 establishes the setup (same concern noted by task 11)
LearnPanel.test.tsx is flagged as 'undeclared' by the scope check (warning, not failure) — cosmetic, same as task 11
